prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1366; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right-hand lane of the roadway in League City, Texas, when the vehicle operated by Driver 2 struck the rear of Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 2 reported that the vehicle was slowing for traffic when the impact occurred. Driver 1 was seated behind the wheel at the time of the collision, and a Passenger was also present in the vehicle. Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash and stated that the head and neck were thrown forward and back during the impact. The force of the collision and the position of both vehicles are consistent with that type of injury. Responding officers took photographs of both vehicles, which confirm the general location of the damage. No independent witnesses to the collision were identified at the scene. Officers could not determine with certainty whether all of the damage to Driver 1's vehicle resulted from this impact. No prior damage to the vehicle was known to the officers or reported by either driver. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the applicable policy.
